Actually, if `n == oo`, we just want to avoid returning something that's likely wrong because of `oo/oo`.

If `n == oo`, the product `Product(p/q, (k, a, oo))` converges only if `p/q -> 1`.
If `p` and `q` are polynomials, `p/q -> 1` means they have the same leading coefficient and degree.
In that case, both `_eval_product(p, ...)` and `_eval_product(q, ...)` will diverge to `oo` (or 0).

So if `n == oo`, and `_eval_product(p, ...)` and `_eval_product(q, ...)` both return something that's not a finite number, we are in this problematic case.
